newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon slowdown temporary - c.bank governor.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon slowdown temporary - c.bank governor.

text.p: Lebanon's current economic slowdown is temporary and is caused by a construction slump and other seasonal causes, Bank of Lebanon Governor Riad Salameh said on Wednesday.

"The economic slowdown which Lebanon has experienced since September 1996 will be temporary and it is caused by the decline of the construction industry and by other seasonal causes," Salameh told Arab bankers and financiers at a conference in Beirut. He gave no further details.
The central bank has previously estimated 1996 GDP growth at four percent -- well down from the 6.5-seven percent estimated for 1995.

The private sector construction industry, which underwent a post-civil war boom until 1995, has slowed drastically since then due to market saturation with many new buildings in Beirut and other regions standing empty.
